proposals: DPIIT should publish an annual table mapping India’s largest import chapters by value to the central schemes that target each one, with outlay and status, so a scheme’s absence from PIB’s achievement recaps, as with NMEO-Oilseeds and the DAP supply deals, is not mistaken for absence of policy.

The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals should publish an import-dependence assessment for plastics (HS39) and inorganic chemicals (HS28), stating which schemes, if any, address them, since together they exceed $36 billion of imports and grew 45.8% and 86.0% with no scheme identifiable in the window.

The Department of Fertilizers should report each year the urea capacity commissioned under NIPU-2026 against its roughly 1 crore tonne target, alongside urea imports, so whether the new policy actually closes the 10-million-tonne gap can be tracked plant by plant.

The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare should publish annual progress under the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oilseeds against its 72% self-sufficiency target for 2030–31, so the ₹10,103 crore mission can be read against HS15 imports that grew 97.9%.
